newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Leading Swedish business figures Svanholm dies.
newsitem.headline: Leading Swedish business figures Svanholm dies.

text.p: A top Swedish business leader, Bert-Olof Svanholm, died on Tuesday, at the age of 62.
Svanholm had been chairman of vehicle maker AB Volvo since 1994 and chairman of the Confederation of Swedish Industries since 1995.
He was managing director of Sweden's ABB at the time of the merger between Asea and Brown Boveri in 1988.
Svanholm had been ill for some time and had already decided to stand down as chairman of the confederation at its annual meeting on April 16.
"Sweden's business sector has lost an outstanding leader," Percy Barnevik, chairman of international engineer ABB, said in a statement.
"He cleverly managed to combine commercial company leadership with a deep insight into how one could improve an organisation through developing and investing in individuals in an organisation."
Volvo's board said Svanholm would be deeply missed.
"His long industrial experience has been invaluable to Volvo," Volvo said in a statement. "We deeply regret his death which also means the loss of a strong figure in Swedish business."

In recent weeks Svanholm headed a group of 102 business leaders in a battle against the current government, saying its economic policies and agreement to phase out Sweden's nuclear power industry was not supporting the business community.
